The Optimist Daily podcast discusses a study showing that people consistently underestimate the willingness of others to cooperate, despite 69% of participants choosing to help strangers at a cost.

The Poison:
While the study is hopeful, it doesn't address why our *perception* of others remains so cynical, which is the real driver of modern division.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
No plane error. The WHO (the study participants) and the WHAT (the cooperation experiment) are clearly defined.

Social Physics Analysis:
By highlighting our innate tendency to cooperate, the podcast reduces the 'cynicism tax' that prevents people from working together. It promotes transparency over the projection of bad motives.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. The data aligns with the message, creating a stable, positive feedback loop.

The Unavoidable Truth: We are more cooperative than our cynical media landscape leads us to believe.

The Unavoidable Lie: That our individual cooperation is enough to fix systemic, institutionalized division.

Alethekanon:
This is a rare instance of 'Good Preference' being supported by empirical data. It effectively counters the 'projection' loop that fuels modern political polarization.

It warms my heart to know that deep down, we really do want to help each other. We just need to start trusting that the person next to us feels the same way.
